clue.text: This tube, blown, will make the pulse race

definitions.text: This tube, blown, will make the pulse race

parts.words: This tube, blown, will make the pulse race
parts.note: sounds like excitement, but the pulse is a pea, a pulse vegetable, sent speeding out of a toy tube by a puff of breath

explanation.surface: Something thrilling, maybe a trumpet, that sets the heart pounding.
explanation.definitionFit: A child's toy tube fires dried peas, which are pulses, when someone blows through it.

clue.text: Places outside tradesmen's entrance for taps

indicators.note: one word placed outside another wraps round it

parts.note: to put means to place

indicators.note: the entrance of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Where to position things outside the trade entrance, in search of taps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entrance' takes the T of tradesmen's, and 'outside' wraps PUTS round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Putts are gentle strokes in golf, light knocks of the ball towards the hole.

clue.text: Taut getting out of taxi (automatic)? That is self-evident

indicators.note: the letters of taut leave the phrase, as a passenger gets out of a cab

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone tense climbing out of an automatic cab, with an obvious remark.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove T, A, U, T in order from TAXIAUTOMATIC; 'That is' joins.
explanation.definitionFit: An axiom is a truth accepted without proof, so axiomatic means obvious.

clue.text: Heaps that made horse stumble in this recreation area

indicators.note: a stumble throws things out of order, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
horse is slang for heroin, abbreviated H

explanation.surface: Piles of something tripping up a horse in a park.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stumble' rearranges HEAPSTHATMADE plus H. Hampstead Heath is a large open park in north London.
explanation.definitionFit: This London heath is a vast public open space for walking and leisure.

clue.text: Heart of Midlothian greeting in play

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its central letters

parts.note: hello is a greeting

explanation.surface: A Scottish football fan saying hi at the theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heart of' takes the central OT of Midlothian. Heart of Midlothian is an Edinburgh football club, which misleads.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare wrote this tragedy about the Moor of Venice.

clue.text: Sigh for a spoken version of Morse, for example

annotationWithheld.why: Sigh for a spoken version of Morse, for example (7): 'Morse, for example' defines ENCODER, but no parse of 'Sigh for a spoken version' giving the letters was found
annotationWithheld.clue: Sigh for a spoken version of Morse, for example

clue.text: Fuel is undervalued to some extent

indicators.note: only part of the word undervalued is used, so the letters sit inside it

explanation.surface: A complaint that some fuel is priced too cheaply.
explanation.definitionFit: Derv is British slang for diesel oil used in road vehicles.

clue.text: Lamb, stuffed with top of zedoary, is Higgins' favourite

indicators.note: one piece is filled with another, so a letter goes inside

parts.note: Elia was the pen name of the essayist Charles Lamb

indicators.note: the top of a word in a down clue is its first letter

explanation.surface: Roast lamb stuffed with a spice, a professor's favourite dish.
explanation.walkthrough: Zedoary is a ginger-like spice. Professor Higgins tutors Eliza Doolittle in Pygmalion and My Fair Lady.
explanation.definitionFit: Eliza Doolittle is the flower girl whom the phonetics professor trains and grows fond of.

clue.text: Unofficial policeman leaving, it turns out

indicators.note: something turned out is reshaped, so the letters of leaving and it are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A policeman, it emerges, is quitting the force.
explanation.definitionFit: A vigilante takes the law into their own hands without legal authority.

clue.text: Light sauce — something to attract passing customers?

parts.note: a window lets in light, and light is an old word for a window pane
a dressing is a sauce for salad

explanation.surface: A light sauce on a menu, offered as a lure for diners.
explanation.definitionFit: Shop displays arranged behind glass entice people walking by to step in.

clue.text: Rump hit playfully in exultation

indicators.note: doing something playfully suggests messing about, so the letters of rump and hit are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone smacks a backside in a fit of glee.
explanation.definitionFit: Triumph is the feeling of great joy at a victory, a synonym for elation.

clue.text: Reported settling of upper limit on prices

indicators.note: something reported is spoken out, so the word for settling is heard rather than written

parts.note: sealing a deal means settling it

explanation.surface: A news item about agreeing a cap on what shops may charge.
explanation.walkthrough: SEALING, as in sealing a bargain, is said like CEILING.
explanation.definitionFit: A price ceiling is a maximum level set by authority that charges cannot exceed.

clue.text: Adhesive sticking concrete on house

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece placed on another sits right beside it

parts.note: a semi is a semi-detached house
concrete means solid, real and tangible

explanation.surface: Glue being stuck onto the concrete of a house.
explanation.walkthrough: SEMI is British shorthand for a semi-detached house, one sharing a wall with its neighbour; 'sticking' merely joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Glues and pastes are typically half liquid and half firm, thick but not set.

clue.text: Write at length and speak the same way

parts.note: to draw a cheque is to write it out

explanation.surface: An instruction to write long-windedly and talk in the same long-winded way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the same way' means at length: to speak slowly, drawing the words out.
explanation.definitionFit: A drawl is slow speech with long-stretched vowels, as when someone talks lazily.

clue.text: It must be returned before the tenth

indicators.note: returning something sends it back the way it came, so the word it is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A library-style reminder that something is due back before the tenth of the month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'before the' looks like part of a date; THE is a piece and 'tenth' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A tithe was a tenth of produce or income paid to the church.

clue.text: Victorian fare-carrier, possibly?

parts.note: suggests a cab from the 1800s, but means a food sack used by someone in the Australian state of Victoria

explanation.surface: A nineteenth-century cab or bus taking paying passengers.
explanation.walkthrough: Tucker is Australian slang for food, so fare is food, not a passenger's payment.
explanation.definitionFit: An Australian bushman's food bag holds provisions, which is fare in the sense of meals.

clue.text: F-fours possibly?

parts.note: reads like a paper size or a jet name, but means female fours, the women crewing a four-person rowing boat

explanation.surface: A stuttered mention of fours, perhaps fighter jets.
explanation.definitionFit: Female rowers make up a women's four in rowing races.

clue.text: St Paul's in this state!

parts.note: suggests the London cathedral in a bad condition, but St Paul is a city, the capital of a US state

explanation.surface: An exclamation about the cathedral being in a sorry mess.
explanation.definitionFit: Saint Paul is the capital of this Midwestern American state.

clue.text: Commanding officer in Macedon shaking off evil spirit

indicators.note: one piece goes in the other, so the officer's abbreviation sits inside
shaking things up disturbs their order, so the letters of Macedon are jumbled

explanation.surface: An army officer in ancient Macedon throwing off a demon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shaking off' reads like an exorcism but signals the jumble (CADEMON from Macedon); 'in' puts the officer inside it, after the opening CA.
explanation.definitionFit: A cacodemon is a malevolent demon, from Greek kakos, bad.

clue.text: The sea engulfing taxi? How gruesome

indicators.note: to engulf is to swallow up, so the word for taxi goes inside

parts.note: mare is Latin for sea, as in the lunar seas
a cab is a taxi

explanation.surface: Waves swallowing a cab, a horrifying sight.
explanation.definitionFit: Macabre means ghastly and preoccupied with death.

clue.text: Half-nelson on boss in the plant

indicators.note: half of a word here means its first half, the opening three letters

parts.note: an umbo is the raised boss at the centre of a shield

explanation.surface: A wrestler puts a hold on the boss in the factory.
explanation.walkthrough: A half-nelson is a wrestling hold; plant means a factory in the surface. Nelumbo is the lotus genus.
explanation.definitionFit: Nelumbo is the genus of water lilies including the sacred lotus.

clue.text: The limits of a large stove

explanation.surface: The boundaries of an enormous cooker.
explanation.definitionFit: Range means the extent or reach of something, and is also a big kitchen cooking oven with hotplates.

clue.text: Excellent hole for a bird

explanation.surface: A fine hole for a bird to nest in.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf, two strokes under par on a hole is a superb score; it is also a large bird of prey.

clue.text: Position in form in America

explanation.surface: A rank held in an American school class.
explanation.definitionFit: Grade means a rank or level, and in American schools a year group, what British schools call a form.

clue.text: Muses cool off in this big theatre

indicators.note: something off has gone wrong, so the letters of muses and cool are disordered

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: The Muses lose interest in a large theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges MUSESCOOL. The London Coliseum is spelt differently; this is the Roman amphitheatre.
explanation.definitionFit: The Colosseum in Rome is a vast ancient amphitheatre for public spectacles.

clue.text: Runs into Hunts, say?

explanation.surface: Someone bumps into hunting parties.
explanation.definitionFit: Meets means encounters by chance, and in fox hunting a meet is a gathering of riders and hounds before the chase.

clue.text: Wherein dippers may be lucky?

parts.note: dippers sound like birds or swimmers, but are children plunging hands into husks to pull out a prize

explanation.surface: A question about where diving birds might find good fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: A tub of bran with small prizes buried in it is a British fairground lucky dip.
explanation.definitionFit: Children at fairs rummage in a container of cereal husks hoping to find a hidden gift.

clue.text: Gold coin needed for suit in watered silk

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other, so the word for suit sits within the fabric

parts.note: moire is silk with a wavy watered finish
to do is to suit or serve, as in that will do

explanation.surface: Money needed to buy a suit of shimmering silk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needed for' joins; 'suit' means DO, not clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A moidore was a Portuguese gold piece current in Britain in the eighteenth century.

clue.text: Delight in unaccompanied song

explanation.surface: Joy found in singing without instruments.
explanation.definitionFit: Glee means great joy, and is also a part-song for several voices without accompaniment.

clue.text: Fragrant oil no real answer to marijuana

parts.note: a lemon is a dud, something that fails to work
grass is slang for marijuana

explanation.surface: Scented oil is no real substitute for cannabis.
explanation.definitionFit: This tropical herb yields an aromatic essential oil used in perfumes and cooking.
